proposed_edges.relationship: Four questions put to White (1993): whether a determinist theory of language fits the freedom White grants historians, whether his tropology should itself be historicised, what becomes of research's “heavy and demanding operations”, and how his relativism answers the Shoah and its deniers, as White restates them in his rejoinder
proposed_edges.map_label: Chartier’s four questions to White, 1993, as White restates them
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Chartier's article ("Quatre questions à Hayden White", Storia della Storiografia 24, 1993, 133–142) is unread. The four questions are known through White's 1995 rejoinder, read in full in its authorised Portuguese translation (Revista de Teoria da História 28, 2025, published 14 April 2026): (1) whether it is "contraditório" to invoke a post-Saussurean, "determinista" theory of language while granting historians a poet's freedom (p. 4); (2) whether he treated one tropology as inherent to Western consciousness instead of contextualising the historians' discourses (p. 5); (3) how to regard "opérations très lourdes et exigeantes que sont la constitution d'un corpus documentaire, le contrôle des données et des hypothèses, la construction d'interprétation" (Chartier's French, quoted by White, p. 6); (4) how White's "relativismo" meets the demand for truth raised by the "crimes commis par les tyrannies ou, plus encore, la Shoah" and by revisionist denial (pp. 7–8). Metadata of both articles from Domańska's bibliography. White calls the exchange friendly (p. 4); a critique of Metahistory's assumptions, not a rejection of White's work as a whole.

proposed_edges.relationship: White’s rejoinder (1995): no contradiction between linguistic codes that limit what can be said and freely chosen codes; his tropology was dominant in Western discourse from the late Renaissance; much of erudition’s apparatus is a ritual “theatre” of good faith; Holocaust denial raises no methodological question
proposed_edges.evidence_note: White's own words, read in full in the authorised Portuguese translation (Revista de Teoria da História 28, 2025, e83664, published 14 April 2026; English renderings are atlas translations from Portuguese; the 1995 English original, Storia della Storiografia 27, 63–70, not seen). "Eu estava falando de discursos, não do cosmos" (p. 4); the fourfold tropology was "culturalmente dominante no Ocidente desde o final do Renascimento até o Modernismo", and "O modelo talvez tenha sido menos útil do que eu imaginava; não foi muito bem recebido. Mas era melhor, penso eu, do que não ter modelo nenhum" (p. 5); "A tradução das coisas da realidade em coisas do discurso é uma ficcionalização" and much of the operations Chartier names "pertence ao “teatro” da erudição acadêmica; tem uma função ritual" (pp. 6–7); the deniers "simplesmente (e de forma bastante perversa) negam a ocorrência de certos eventos", and "Não há qualquer questão metodológica em jogo" (pp. 7–8). A reply within a courteous exchange (p. 4), including a concession about his model's reception.

proposed_edges.relationship: Practices are not reducible to discourse: the logic of discourses differs from the logic of conduct, social positions are conditions of possibility of discourse, and cultural historians have moved away from “the illusions of the linguistic turn” (2003)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: His own words, read in full (Cahiers du CRH 31, 2003, OpenEdition; paragraphs cited). The linguistic turn holds "que la « réalité » n'est pas une référence objective, extérieure au discours"; against it, accessing past practices through texts does not mean "affirmer l'identité de deux logiques" (¶25). Social positions "ne sont pas seulement un effet des discours ; elles en désignent également les conditions de possibilité" (¶26). Cultural historians "se sont éloignés tant des illusions du tournant linguistique que des héritages contraignants qui postulaient le primat du politique ou la toute-puissance du social" (¶31). Foucault's own distinction between discursive formations and non-discursive systems is one of his resources (¶25 n. 25), so this is a critique of a position, not of every author grouped under this entry; Hayden White is not named in the article.

proposed_edges.relationship: Doubts the coherence Hunt claimed for the new cultural history in 1989: by 2003 it is held together by shared questions and debate rather than by a unified approach
proposed_edges.map_label: Doubting a unified new cultural history, 2003
proposed_edges.evidence_note: His own words, read in full (Cahiers du CRH 31, 2003). He starts from Hunt's 1989 volume and its three defining traits (¶1–3) and endorses her emphasis on sexual identities as "l'un des traits originaux de la new cultural history" (¶30). Then: "La cohérence la new cultural history est-elle aussi forte que le proclamait Lynn Hunt ? La diversité des objets de recherche, des perspectives méthodologiques et des références théoriques … permet d'en douter"; the field "n'est pas, ou n'est plus, définie par l'unité de son approche, mais par l'espace d'échanges et de débats" (¶31). A bounded disagreement about one claim, within an account that adopts her categories; not a rejection of her work.

proposed_edges.relationship: Bourdieu’s distinction between practical sense and scholastic reason (cited 2003) and his account of social difference (2007 dialogue); Certeau restored the space of readers’ appropriation, though Chartier rejects reading his “poaching” as absolute freedom
proposed_edges.evidence_note: His own words. 2003 article, read in full: to think "cette irréductibilité de l'expérience au discours", historians could rely on Foucault's distinction and on "celle établie par Bourdieu entre « sens pratique » et « raison scolastique »" (¶25, n. 26: Méditations pascaliennes, 1997). 2007 dialogue with Darnton, read in part in Portuguese translation (MATRIZes 5:2, 2012): social difference "não decorre apenas dessa tradição da história social da Annales, decorre também … ao trabalho de Pierre Bourdieu" (p. 164); no contradiction between Bourdieu's sociology of cultural production and McKenzie's sociology of texts (p. 166); "De Certeau, entre outros, restituiu este espaço" between constraints and readers' appropriation, but "seria um erro acreditar que esta liberdade é absoluta" (p. 167). In 1988 he recorded five radio dialogues with Bourdieu, published as a book in 2010 (presentation, p. 162; Prismas bibliography). Named resources with qualifications, not adherence to a school.

proposed_edges.relationship: Later studies of the mobility of texts across attributions, printed versions, forms of publication, genres and translations: the lost Cardenio between Cervantes and Shakespeare (2011) and Éditer et traduire (2021), in their reviewers’ accounts
proposed_edges.map_label: The mobility of texts, 2011–2021, per reviewers
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Mediated: the books are unread. Boucheron's review of Cardenio (Books & Ideas, 2014; consulted through WebFetch extraction; selected quoted passages recorded; full text not collated): its problem is "the discrepancy between the mobility of texts and the stability of authorial names"; Boucheron expects the claim that the author function took its final form in the eighteenth century to "provoke debate, particularly among Medievalists": an anticipated objection, not a later controversy investigated here. Jouhaud (Prismas 26, 2022, pp. 236–237, read) quotes Éditer et traduire on "las cinco modalidades que suministran a las obras su movilidad" (attribution, printed variants, forms of publication, genres, translation). Chartier's own 2020–2021 Collège de France report (read via WebFetch extraction) describes research "vouées à comprendre les raisons de la mobilité des textes". Prismas's bibliography dates the books (2011; 2021). A contribution to the history of publishing and circulation within intellectual history; Darnton's separate strand membership is unchanged.

new_sources.citation: Roger Chartier, « La nouvelle histoire culturelle existe-t-elle ? », Les Cahiers du Centre de Recherches Historiques 31 (2003), online 15 September 2008.

verification.note: Read in full for revision 1.147 in the OpenEdition HTML (paragraphs 1–31 and notes; no print pagination, so paragraphs are cited). ¶1: the category entered historians' common vocabulary when Lynn Hunt published her 1989 volume. ¶11: the critique of mentalités "était peut-être injuste"; shared demands: individual uses over statistical distributions, "les modalités spécifiques de leur appropriation", representations of the social world as constitutive of differences and struggles. ¶12: the risk of "une définition impérialiste de la catégorie". ¶19: forms "participent, elles aussi, à la construction de leur signification". ¶24: "C'est dans cet écart que s'insinuent reformulations et détournements, appropriations et résistances." ¶25: the linguistic turn holds "que la « réalité » n'est pas une référence objective, extérieure au discours"; against it, the logic of discourses and the logic of conduct are not identical; historians can rely on Foucault's distinction between "« formations discursives » et « systèmes non discursifs »" (n. 25) and Bourdieu's between "« sens pratique » et « raison scolastique »" (n. 26, Méditations pascaliennes, 1997); n. 24 cites Keith Baker for the linguistic-turn position. ¶26: social positions "ne sont pas seulement un effet des discours ; elles en désignent également les conditions de possibilité." ¶28: representation "en est presque venu à désigner en lui-même la nouvelle histoire culturelle". ¶31: "La cohérence la new cultural history est-elle aussi forte que le proclamait Lynn Hunt ? La diversité … permet d'en douter"; the field is defined "par l'espace d'échanges et de débats" among historians who refuse to reduce phenomena to one dimension and "se sont éloignés tant des illusions du tournant linguistique que des héritages contraignants qui postulaient le primat du politique ou la toute-puissance du social." Hayden White is not named. Also published in Francia 33/2 (2006), not read in that form.

new_sources.citation: Hayden White, “A Rejoinder: A Response to Professor Chartier’s Four Questions,” Storia della Storiografia 27 (1995): 63–70; Portuguese translation by Hugo Merlo, Revista de Teoria da História 28 (2025), e83664, published 14 April 2026.

verification.note: Read in full for revision 1.147 in the journal's PDF (13 pp.): translator's presentation pp. 1–3 and the rejoinder pp. 4–13, in Portuguese; the 1995 English original was not seen, so English renderings here are translations from the Portuguese. The translation is published with the permission of the Brose-White Trust and the Hayden White Literary Estate (p. 1 n. 1). Chartier's 1993 article ("Quatre questions à Hayden White", Storia della Storiografia 24, 1993, 133–142) is unread; its questions are known only as White restates them and through the French phrases he quotes. The debate ran in Storia della Storiografia "entre 1993 e 1995" (translator, p. 2). Q1 (p. 4): whether it is "contraditório" to invoke a determinist theory of language and grant historians a poet's freedom; White: "Eu estava falando de discursos, não do cosmos." Q2 (p. 5): whether tropology should be historicised; White: the fourfold model was culturally dominant from the late Renaissance to Modernism, and "O modelo talvez tenha sido menos útil do que eu imaginava; não foi muito bem recebido." Q3 (pp. 6–7): what becomes of the "opérations très lourdes et exigeantes que sont la constitution d'un corpus documentaire, le contrôle des données et des hypothèses, la construction d'interprétation" (Chartier's French as White quotes it); White: they belong largely to the "teatro" of scholarship and have "uma função ritual". Q4 (pp. 7–8): how his relativism answers the crimes of tyrannies and "plus encore, la Shoah" and revisionist denial; White: the deniers "negam a ocorrência de certos eventos" and "Não há qualquer questão metodológica em jogo". White thanks Chartier for discussing "amigavelmente" (p. 4). Dates: the journal page assigns the translation to volume 28 (2025) and gives its publication date as 14 April 2026 (rechecked 2026-10-19); 2025 is the volume year, not an established posting date. The original rejoinder is 1995.

verification.note: Consulted through WebFetch extraction for revision 1.147; selected quoted passages recorded; full text not collated (no pagination). Jouhaud quotes the lecture: "le raz de marée de la textualité numérique représente une rupture majeure dans l'histoire de la culture écrite"; "la double nature, matérielle et immatérielle, de l'écrit"; the questions "qu'est-ce qu'un livre ? qu'est-ce qu'un auteur ? qu'est-ce qu'un texte ? quelle autorité pour l'écrit ?"; and the aim to "repérer les durées sédimentées de la culture écrite pour comprendre plus justement les mutations". His judgement: "nul ne l'a mieux affirmé, démontré et enseigné que Roger Chartier". Descriptive and admiring; no criticism.

verification.note: Read in part for revision 1.147 (open-access PDF from the USP journal): presentation pp. 159–162 and Darnton's questions II–IV with Chartier's answers, pp. 164–167, in Portuguese translation; p. 163 (the first question and answer) is not cited. Chartier: social difference "não decorre apenas dessa tradição da história social da Annales, decorre também … ao trabalho de Pierre Bourdieu" (p. 164); "pode-se considerar as diferenças entre os sexos como uma diferença social" (p. 164); no "relações imediatas, mecânicas, entre meios sociais e práticas culturais" (p. 165); no contradiction between Bourdieu's sociology of cultural production and McKenzie's sociology of texts (p. 166); between determinism of form and the reader's absolute freedom, "limitação transgredida e liberdade cerceada"; "De Certeau, entre outros, restituiu este espaço" between constraints and readers' appropriation, but "seria um erro acreditar que esta liberdade é absoluta", an "uso infeliz" of the essay on reading as poaching (p. 167).

The book "adopts the style and format of an investigation" and opens with the court performance of winter 1612–1613; its problem is "the discrepancy between the mobility of texts and the stability of authorial names"; Theobald's Double Falshood (1727) is examined as possibly the "only surviving textual trace"; Boucheron reports Chartier's view that the Foucauldian author function reached its "final form" in the eighteenth century and adds that "This assertion will undoubtedly provoke debate, particularly among Medievalists" (an anticipated objection); "an historical essay that is in many respects experimental".
